item.title: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle: Japan's Highest Original Keep — Guide
item.description: Bitchu Matsuyama is unique: of Japan’s twelve surviving original castle keeps, it is the only one still standing on a mountain top, at 430 metres above the town of Takahashi. Built and rebuilt from the 13th century onwards, the present keep dates from 1683 and has never been reconstructed — you climb to a genuinely old wooden building, small and weathered, set among massive stone ramparts and rock outcrops that follow the ridge.

item.title: Takeda Castle Ruins: The Castle in the Sea of Clouds — Guide
item.description: Takeda Castle is one of Japan’s most photographed ruins, and deservedly so. Built in the 15th century on a narrow ridge 353 metres above the Asago valley and abandoned around 1600, all that survives is its remarkable stonework — tiers of ramparts, bailey walls and gate foundations tracing the whole plan of the castle along the mountaintop. On calm, cold mornings in autumn, mist pools in the valley below and the ruins stand clear above a white sea of cloud, an image that has earned it the nicknames ‘Japan’s Machu Picchu’ and ‘the castle in the sky’.
